headline: Gulf Coast Access and Everglades Permitting
reservation: While public beaches in Naples do not require reservations, parking is the primary bottleneck and often requires early arrival or a city-issued permit. Visiting nearby Big Cypress or the Everglades may require specific activity permits for airboats or backcountry camping; check the official National Park Service sites for current seasonal water levels and access restrictions. Accommodation in the peak winter season should be secured several months in advance.

days.title: White Sands and Historic Piers
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Fifth Avenue South

stops.name: Naples Pier
stops.detail: Walk this 1888 landmark for fishing and dolphin spotting over the Gulf of Mexico's calm waters.

stops.name: Third Street South Historic District
stops.detail: Explore the original heart of the town, featuring Mediterranean-style architecture and landscaped courtyards.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; very walkable within the downtown grid
days.note: Beach parking meters are strictly enforced; use official apps for payments.

days.title: Mangroves and Wilderness Boardwalks

stops.name: Delnor-Wiggins Pass State Park
stops.detail: Swim or shell on one of the most pristine barrier islands on the Gulf Coast, separated by a natural mangrove estuary.

stops.name: Audubon Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary
stops.detail: Walk the 2.25-mile boardwalk through the world’s largest remaining stand of old-growth bald cypress trees.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours; traffic on Tamiami Trail varies by time of day
days.note: Check mosquito activity levels at Corkscrew Swamp before starting your walk.

days.title: Exotic Gardens and Botanical Beauty

stops.name: Naples Zoo at Caribbean Gardens
stops.detail: See exotic animals within a historic botanical garden first planted in 1919.

stops.name: Naples Botanical Garden
stops.detail: Explore 170 acres of tropical plants representing the flora of the tropics across the globe.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; sites are situated on the eastern edge of the city
days.note: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer; plan outdoor zoo visits for the morning.

intel.title: Everglades Entry
intel.text: Access to Big Cypress and the Everglades via the Tamiami Trail is straightforward, but certain boardwalks may close during the summer wet season. Verify water levels on the NPS website if planning a swamp walk.

intel.title: Tamiami Trail Services
intel.text: Gas stations are plentiful in Naples proper but become non-existent for long stretches once you enter the Big Cypress National Preserve. Fuel up before heading east toward Miami or south toward Flamingo.

intel.title: Beachfront Capacity
intel.text: Low-dermilk Park and Pier parking usually fill by 10 AM during the winter peak. Use the parking garage downtown and walk several blocks to the beach to avoid traffic loops.

intel.title: Wilderness Gaps
intel.text: Cellular coverage is excellent in Naples and Marco Island but disappears almost entirely within the deep cypress stands of the Everglades. Ensure you have physical maps for navigation in the preserve.

intel.title: Shelling Cycles
intel.text: The best shelling at Delnor-Wiggins occurs after a storm or during low tide. Consult a local tide chart to time your beach walk for the best mineral finds.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Southwest Florida International Airport (RSW); pick up your rental car and stock up on supplies in Fort Myers or Naples before heading to your coastal hotel.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for city and main preserve roads; check rental terms for off-road swamp access.
plan.goldenHour: Naples Pier provides a clear horizon for Gulf sunsets; the 'green flash' is a rare seasonal possibility.
